title: a temporary source lives as a bound one; each cursor owns its own resource for one step; a shared one goes once
purpose: Observe failure, cleanup and lifetime ordering during execution.

stdout.text:
plain temporary: +src i0(src,src) body0 i1(src,src) body1 i2(src,src) body2 after -src
plain bound:     +src i0(src,src) body0 i1(src,src) body1 i2(src,src) body2 after -src
fresh temporary: +src +c0 i0(src,c0) body0 +c1 -c0 i1(src,c1) body1 +c2 -c1 i2(src,c2) body2 +c3 -c2 -c3 after -src
fresh bound:     +src +c0 i0(src,c0) body0 +c1 -c0 i1(src,c1) body1 +c2 -c1 i2(src,c2) body2 +c3 -c2 -c3 after -src
shared temporary: +src +shared i0(src,shared) body0 i1(src,shared) body1 i2(src,shared) body2 -shared after -src
shared bound:     +src +shared i0(src,shared) body0 i1(src,shared) body1 i2(src,shared) body2 -shared after -src

provenance.origin: authored for #483/#484 from the cited contract text
provenance.expected_basis: #483/#484: the scope of the loop owns the temporary source like a let; each step owns its cursor, the next step takes the new one, and a superseded cursor and what only it reached are destroyed once (+c1 -c0); a resource shared by all cursors goes when the last cursor does, before the code after the loop.
